summary: For ages 6-7 (Y2), help children understand that the multiples of 10 (10, 20, 30 … 90) each represent a whole number of tens with zero ones — e.g. 30 is 3 tens and 0 ones. The key insight is that the 0 in a decade is an active place-holder marking the empty ones column, not 'nothing', and that decades are simply the 'whole tens, no ones' case of ordinary two-digit place value. Build quantities with tens rods, anchor to skip-counting in tens, and contrast a decade with a nearby non-decade so the 0 earns its meaning.
misconceptions: Treating the 0 in a decade as meaningless ('nothing there') rather than as a place-holder marking zero ones.
Reading the tens digit as its face value — saying 30 is 'three' rather than 'three tens/thirty'.
Decade-word confusion — mixing thirteen with thirty, fifteen with fifty, because the '-teen' and '-ty' endings sound alike.
Believing decades are a separate kind of number unrelated to ordinary two-digit numbers, rather than the ones-is-zero case of tens-and-ones.
Miscounting the rods and losing track that each rod is worth ten, not one, when skip-counting.

activities.title: Building decades with tens rods and a visible zero
steps: Set up a tens|ones chart (drawn or physical) with two columns.
Add tens rods one at a time into the tens column, placing no unit cubes; after each rod, say the count aloud: 'ten, twenty, thirty …' and write the numeral (10, 20, 30).
Each time, write a 0 in the ones column so the empty ones place is seen, not left blank.
Build 30 with three rods and say '30 is 3 tens and 0 ones'; build 50 with five rods and say '50 is 5 tens and 0 ones'.
Rebuild 30 with three rods, then add a single loose ones cube and read what you have: 30 becomes 31. Describe what the 0 was doing before you added the cube.
Optionally mark each decade on a 0-100 number line or bead string so the spoken word, the tens count, and the position all line up.
activities.insight: A decade is a whole number of tens with the ones column filled by zero; the 0 is a place-holder that keeps the tens digit in the tens place and marks that there are no ones. Decades are not a separate kind of number — they are the ones-is-zero case of tens-and-ones.

activities.title: Decade reference chart — tap, reveal, and lift the flap
steps: Work from a chart of the nine decades (10, 20 … 90).
For a chosen decade (e.g. 30), reveal its three tens rods, the words '3 tens, 0 ones', and the spoken name 'thirty'.
Use a 'where did the ones go?' prompt (e.g. a lift-the-flap or cover) to answer: there are zero ones, and the 0 marks that.
Read across several decades to notice that reading only the tens column gives the decade name.
activities.insight: Each decade numeral maps to a count of tens, a decade name (ten, or a '-ty' word from twenty to ninety), and a zero in the ones column; the tens digit tells you which decade it is.

activities.title: Consolidation: sequence, match, and justify the zero
steps: Put the decade numerals in order smallest to largest (10, 20 … 90).
Match each decade numeral to a picture of the correct number of tens rods.
Fill in blanks such as '30 = __ tens' and '50 = 5 tens and __ ones'.
Choose and explain the meaning of the 0 in a decade (zero ones / place-holder), not 'nothing'.
Distinguish sound-alike pairs: thirteen vs thirty, fifteen vs fifty — say which is 'teen' (ten and some) and which is 'ty' (whole tens).
activities.insight: Children can recognise and justify decades across different representations, and can avoid confusing '-teen' words with '-ty' words.

activities.title: 'Convince me the zero matters' discussion
steps: Discuss the question: 'Why does 30 need a zero? What would happen if we just wrote 3?'
Use rods or a chart to argue your case: show that without the 0, the 3 would sit in the ones place and mean three.
Explain to a partner or adult why 30 is not the same as 3, and what the 0 is holding.
activities.insight: Articulating the reason makes the place-holder role of the 0 explicit: it keeps the 3 in the tens place and marks zero ones.

checkQuestion: Write 30. Point to the 3, then the 0. Ask: 'What is the 3 telling us, and what is the 0 telling us? How do you know?'
checkAnswer: The 3 means 3 tens; the 0 means there are 0 ones. So 30 is 3 tens and 0 ones.
